skills.content:
---
name: twitch-radio-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation after the Twitch music-radio bot template
  is imported: confirm music rights, get the stream key saved securely, build
  the ffmpeg pipeline, and run a private test.
---
I run your music livestream on Twitch from my computer: a looping set of your own songs with cover art, a waveform visual and a now-playing title. I only go live when you say go.

Ask these one at a time:
1. What's your Twitch channel name, and what should the on-screen brand line say (e.g. "now playing: <title> — <your studio name>")?
2. Where does your music come from (for example your Suno profile or a folder of files)? Is it all your own work? If it was made with an AI music tool, was it made on a paid plan that grants commercial rights? If the answer isn't a clear yes, stop and explain that streaming it risks takedowns.
3. Where's your cover art? Use existing covers only, and don't generate art yourself.
4. Stream key: send a secure secret request named TWITCH_STREAM_KEY. Never ask for it in chat, and never print or log it. If they paste it in chat, tell them to reset it in the Twitch dashboard and resend it securely.

Then:
- Save the channel, brand line and music source as profile memories.
- Build /workspace/radio/ with tracks/ (audio + metadata), playlists, overlay/, stream.sh and LOG.md. Use ffmpeg: 1080p30 (or 720p30) cover art plus a waveform, a lower-third now-playing title per track, x264 CBR ~4500 kbps with a keyframe every 2 s, and 160k AAC. Ingest is rtmp://live.twitch.tv/app/. If port 1935 is blocked, use rtmps://live.twitch.tv:443/app/.
- Run a 2-minute private test with ?bandwidthtest=true on the key. Report the bitrate, dropped frames and audio sync.
- Offer a first session. Go live only on their word, with a length (default 2h).

skills.name: twitch-radio-session
skills.description: Use this when the owner says "go live" for a Twitch music-radio session: run the stream, watch its health, end on time, and report.
skills.content:
---
name: twitch-radio-session
description: >-
  Use this when the owner says "go live" for a Twitch music-radio session: run
  the stream, watch its health, end on time, and report.
---
1. Go live only when the owner says go, with a length or end time (default 2h), or on a schedule they approved in writing. Never run 24/7.
2. Music is the owner's own tracks only. No one else's music, samples or footage (DMCA).
3. Run ffmpeg in the background under a supervisor that survives your turn. Check health every few minutes: speed ~1.0x, fps, dropped frames ≤1%, A/V sync, no silence over 3 s, and the correct now-playing title for every track. Also watch the socket or bytes sent, not just the progress file. A dead connection can leave ffmpeg 'running' with its out_time frozen.
4. On a crash or stall, restart once from the start of the current track. If it fails a second time, stop and report.
5. Never print or log the stream key, and redact it from any command line you capture.
6. Don't change Twitch settings, title or category without asking. Don't chat, raid, DM or post; promo posts belong to the owner or their posting bot. A read-only anonymous chat logger (wss://irc-ws.chat.twitch.tv:443, justinfan nick) is fine.
7. End on time and log the start, end, tracks and errors in LOG.md. Send a short summary: status first (live, offline or blocked), then duration, tracks played, issues and any chat.
